title: Legal Administrator
raw_text:
8-270A. MOS 270A--Legal Administrator
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. In accordance with 10 USC 3037(c) (2), The Judge
Advocate General (TJAG) certifies warrant officers to serve in the JAGC. Certification includes
TJAG’s determination that the initial requirements for accession into the JAGC have been met,
awarding of MOS 270A and maintaining appointment in the JAGC. TJAG’s certification will
ensure that all warrant officers possess and maintain highest levels of ethical and personal
conduct, moral behavior and MOS proficiency. TJAG can evaluate a legal administrator’s
qualifications as needed to include when the warrant officer engages in misconduct that is
detrimental to good order and discipline and TJAG determines revocation of MOS 270A is in the
best interest of the Army.
    b. Prerequisites. DA PAM 611-21.
    c. MOS 270A MOS 270A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is 27D.
    d. Restrictions. No record of conviction by special or general courts-martial or civilian courts of
offenses listed in AR 27-10 (Military Justice), chapter 24 or otherwise required to register as a
sexual offender under AR 27-10, chapter 24.
    e. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    f. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-5 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
warrant officer MOS)).
    g. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Complete the Judge Advocate Warrant Officer Basic Course.
               (b) Complete the Judge Advocate General's School Resident Legal Administrators
Course.
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Advanced Course.
         (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
         (4) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
    h. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2—Performs and/or manages all activities pertaining to the processes and
systems associated with the following core competencies in support of all JAGC Core Legal
Disciplines:
               (a) Legal Systems Integration and Innovation. Performs information management
and systems integration, including protection of government information and attorney-client
privileged information and attorney work product. Analyzes legal systems and processes and
advises senior leader on quality assurance and internal control measures. Develops
requirements and plans and mitigates risk. Facilitates AC/RC integration and partnership
opportunities. Leads change with staff coordination and synchronization including ORSA and
internal review activities. Manages facilities, technology, and logistics in support of legal
operations in garrison and deployed environments across the full spectrum of operations.
               (b) Knowledge Management. Assesses legal organization knowledge and
performance and designs and leads development of solutions to knowledge gaps. Leads
pilot/experimentation and change management initiatives. Performs quality control and quality
assurances activities in support of legal operations.
               (c) Resource management. Provides comprehensive management of all budgetary
resources by determining budgetary requirements, procuring funding, planning and managing
budgets, planning and executing contracts (including expert witnesses), and executing budgets in
 support of legal operations and special programs (including witness travel and special victim
counsel program). Serves as claims investigating officer or on a Foreign Claims Commission in
deployed environments.
               (d) Legal Personnel Management. Manages all aspects of training and continuing
legal education, certification, administration, and readiness of personnel serving in a legal office.
Manages the special legal personnel and organizational programs. Coordinates historian and
protocol activities. Serves as adjutant or assistant adjutant in legal support organizations and
serves a Board Recorder in administrative separation boards (RC only).
               (e) Force Management. Provides force management subject matter expertise by
analyzing and monitoring manpower requirements and current and projected authorizations.
Prepares manpower plans and coordinates force management documentation. Resources
manning documents.
               (f) Security. Serves as security manager for assigned organizations. Responsible for
all security requirements in accordance with applicable regulations including: physical security,
information security, personnel security, communications security (COMSEC), and anti-
terrorism/force protection. Provides Operations Security oversight and plans Continuity of
Operations. Coordinates with military agencies for proper building and personnel security in high-
profile courts-martial cases.
         (2) CW3--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph h(1) with increased knowledge and
expertise. Recruits and assesses potential JAGC warrant officer applicants.
               (b) Provides guidance and technical assistance to subordinate legal elements and/or
other staff elements.
         (3) CW4—
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph h(1)& h(2) and mentors subordinate
JAGC Warrant Officers.
               (b) Educates members of the JAGC through formal programs of instruction.
         (4) CW5--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph h(1), h(2) & h(3).
               (b) Responsible for MOS proponency and career management functions.
               (c) Provides Knowledge Management expertise for the JAG Corps.
    i. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate.
         (2) Table 8-270A-1. Physical requirements.
         (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-270A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-270A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
